extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners in computational humor, conversational AI, and NLP
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and evaluating systems that generate contextually integrated jokes in conversational settings (chatbots/social robots), including symbolic humor algorithms combined with large language models and human evaluation protocols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surprise Theory: three-part monologue joke
rubrics_metrics.description: One of those humor algorithms, derived from the Surprise Theory of Laughter (Toplyn 2021), specifies that a monologue-type joke has these three parts: (a) the topic, (b) the angle, and (c) the punch line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this three-part structure as the high-level framing for constructing a three-part joke (topic → angle → punch line).

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic Joke-Writing Algorithm — Step 1: Select a topic
rubrics_metrics.description: 1. Select a topic. A good joke topic is one sentence that is likely to capture the attention of the audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat an incoming conversational sentence as the topic; prefer concise, attention-getting sentences for easy joke response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic Joke-Writing Algorithm — Step 2: Select two topic handles
rubrics_metrics.description: 2. Select two topic handles. The topic handles are the two words or phrases in the topic that are the most attention-getting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer nouns, noun phrases, or named entities (humor of human-written jokes tends to be based on nouns and noun phrases). Select the two most conspicuous handles to base associations on.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic Joke-Writing Algorithm — Step 3: Generate associations
rubrics_metrics.description: 3. Generate associations of the two topic handles. An association is something that the audience is likely to think of when they think about a particular subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produce lists of likely associations for each handle (e.g., for 'pigs' → bacon, ham; for 'San Antonio' → The Alamo, River Walk) to serve as raw material for punch lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic Joke-Writing Algorithm — Step 4: Create a punch line
rubrics_metrics.description: 4. Create a punch line. The punch line is the word or phrase that results in a laugh. It links an association of one topic handle to an association of the other topic handle in a surprising way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct punch lines by linking associations across handles to create a surprising connection; surprise is central to producing a laugh.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic Joke-Writing Algorithm — Step 5: Generate an angle
rubrics_metrics.description: 5. Generate an angle between the topic and punch line. The angle is a word sequence that connects the topic to the punch line in a natural-sounding way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produce a natural-sounding lead-in (angle) that connects the topic to the punch line so the joke reads/sounds cohesive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generate multiple candidate joke types and select best
rubrics_metrics.description: Witscript 3 links associations of the topic handles in three different ways to create three punch line candidates: a wordplay candidate, a common-sense knowledge candidate, and a third candidate. Then it generates an angle for each and outputs the joke candidate that is most likely the funniest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design systems to produce diverse candidate punch lines (different production mechanisms) and implement a selection stage (e.g., model-based ranking) to choose the funniest output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use specialized phonetic/NLP tools for wordplay creation
rubrics_metrics.description: To create its wordplay candidate, Witscript 3, like Witscript, uses well-known tools of natural language processing to combine one association from each list into a punch line that exhibits wordplay. Witscript 3 does not call on GPT-3 to create its wordplay candidate because GPT-3 seems to be weak at phonetic tasks like generating puns and rhymes, possibly as a result of its use of byte-pair encoding (Branwen 2020).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For phonetic/wordplay tasks (puns, rhymes, phonetic manipulations), rely on phonetic/NLP tools rather than off-the-shelf LLM text generation, which may be weak on such tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use LLMs (GPT-3) for association, common-sense linking, angle generation, and selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Witscript 3 calls the GPT-3 API to select topic handles, generate associations, create common-sense-based punch line candidates, produce angles, and determine which of the joke candidates seems to be the funniest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exploit LLM strengths (common-sense linking, paraphrase/fluency, ranking) by decomposing joke construction into steps and using the LLM for tasks where it performs well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt chaining / stepwise decomposition as a design principle
rubrics_metrics.description: The step-by-step nature of the process results in a system that is more debuggable, editable, controllable, and explainable than an LLM-based system that accomplishes an entire task all at once (prompt chaining).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decompose humor generation into discrete calls (prompt chaining) to improve debuggability, editability, controllability, and explainability; use intermediate outputs as editable artifacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Desiderata for conversational humor modules
rubrics_metrics.description: For a conversational agent to be truly useful, it must be able to generate contextually integrated jokes about what's happening at the moment. What's more, to be high-quality, a conversational agent must generate a variety of jokes using a variety of joke production mechanisms (Amin and Burghardt 2020).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for contextual integration (jokes tied to immediate conversational context) and diversity of production mechanisms (wordplay, common-sense, other strategies) when designing humor modules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation sentence selection criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: I selected sentences from the Topical-Chat dataset using these criteria: (a) its length is 20 words or less; (b) it has no pronouns whose antecedents are unclear; (c) it has at least two nouns, noun phrases, or named entities; and (d) it isn't basically the same as a sentence that has already been selected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When building test inputs for conversational joke generation, filter candidate prompts for brevity, referential clarity, sufficient noun content to support associations, and diversity (avoid near-duplicates).

rubrics_metrics.name: Human evaluator qualifications and procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: AMT workers were required to be located in the United States and have a HIT Approval Rate greater than or equal to 95%. Each of the 39 input/response pairs was evaluated by 15 AMT workers; pairs were put in random order and evaluators were not told how pairs had been obtained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify rater qualifications (location, approval rate), use multiple independent raters per item (here 15), randomize order, and blind raters to source to reduce bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rating scale for humorousness (1–4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluators were asked to rate the response as either 1 (not a joke), 2 (almost a joke), 3 (a joke), or 4 (a very good joke).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use an explicit ordinal scale with category definitions for humorousness so ratings are interpretable; the paper follows a 4-point categorical scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation metrics to report
rubrics_metrics.description: The paper reports mean rating given by evaluators and the percentage of responses rated as 'a joke' or 'a very good joke' (i.e., ratings 3 or 4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report both central tendency (mean rating) and categorical success metrics (percent of outputs judged as jokes) to capture system performance on humor generation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include simple baselines for comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: It introduces a simple joke generator—GPT-LOL—for use as a baseline in evaluating systems that generate conversational jokes. GPT-LOL is GPT-3 (text-davinci-002) prompted: 'You want to be funny. Respond to this: [The sentence].' with Temperature 0.7 and Top P 1.0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear, reproducible baseline (simple prompt-driven LLM) with configuration details so improvements can be quantified against a known reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: System-level goals: scalability, editability, and human collaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: Contributions listed: (1) an automatic, easily scalable system for improvising a variety of contextually integrated jokes that are based on a variety of joke production mechanisms; (3) it demonstrates how an AI system can generate a joke in a series of editable steps, which allows a human to collaborate with the system in creating the joke.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design humor systems to be automatable and scalable, produce varied outputs, structure outputs as editable intermediate artifacts to enable human-in-the-loop collaboration.
